subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which, if any, parts of #35203's four-layer collaboration stack should OpenClaw core own versus plugin, ClawHub, or API-seam ownership?
rationale: The request crosses core agent routing, memory visibility, shared state, cost enforcement, config, and security boundaries, and repository vision is mixed on heavy orchestration layers.

options.title: Keep As Umbrella RFC And Split
options.body: Use #35203 as the canonical design umbrella and require narrow follow-up RFCs or PRs for individual primitives such as capability telemetry, blackboard storage, memory visibility, or budget enforcement.

options.title: Route Optional Coordination To Plugins
options.body: Approve only missing core/plugin APIs and keep optional blackboard, learned routing, and dashboards outside core unless a specific seam is missing.

options.title: Reject Heavy Core Orchestration
options.body: Close the RFC direction as out of roadmap for now and point contributors to existing sessions_spawn, sessions_send, memory search, and usage reporting primitives.

recommendation.title: Keep As Umbrella RFC And Split
recommendation.body: Use #35203 as the canonical design umbrella and require narrow follow-up RFCs or PRs for individual primitives such as capability telemetry, blackboard storage, memory visibility, or budget enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from current source ownership, capability-profile history, and related RFC scoping comments.
